text:
[LEXP.7.15.1] A division, floor-division or modulo whose operands are all
`Int` is a runtime error when the divisor is zero ([LERR.1.4.3]). That includes
`/`, though its result is `Float` ([LEXP.7.4]). Authors who can't rule out zero
denominators guard explicitly. With a `Float` operand, the `Int` one promotes
([LEXP.7.3]) and the operation is IEEE 754's ([LDET.3.6.2]). `/` and `//` give
`±Inf` for a nonzero dividend and NaN for a zero one, and `%` gives NaN.

idris.name: lexp_7_15_1__float_divmod_never_traps
idris.note: With a Float operand `//` and `%` yield a Float for every pair of operands, a zero divisor included, and never a trap, an Int on either side promoted first: the all-Int zero divisor is the one runtime error of the three operators. Which Float the zero row gives (±Inf, NaN) is run in Main.idr.

idris.name: lexp_7_15_1__float_zero_divisor
idris.note: A Float zero divisor, either zero: `//` by it is the IEEE quotient a / b (±Inf for a nonzero dividend, NaN for a zero one) and `%` by it NaN, taken inside `lexp_7_5__float_floordiv` and `lexp_7_6__float_mod` before the composition; run on 5.0 // 0.0, -5.0 // 0.0, 0.0 // 0.0, 5.0 % 0.0, 7 % 0.0 and 7.5 // 0 in Main.idr.

idris.name: lexp_7_15_1__int_zero_divisor_traps
idris.note: For every Int dividend, /, // and % by an Int zero are a trap, `/` included though its result would be a Float. The Float half of the clause is `lexp_7_3__float_op`'s for the three operators, never a trap (`lexp_7_15_1__float_divmod_never_traps`).

idris.name: lexp_7_15_1__zero_divisor
idris.note: Which operators read a divisor, and an Int zero one: /, // and %, with every operand Int. A Float zero divisor is `lexp_7_15_1__float_zero_divisor`'s row.

idris.name: lexp_7_2__int_op
idris.note: A zero divisor under /, // or % is a trap, raised before any division; `/` on two Ints otherwise yields a Float. The evaluator has one trap kind, so [LERR.1.4.3]'s ComputationError is not told from a TypeError; Rete/WhereV5.idr is where kinds live.

idris.name: lexp_7_3__float_op
idris.note: The Float half: with a Float operand the operation is IEEE 754's and a zero divisor gives ±Inf or NaN, never a trap -- `/` directly, `//` and `%` through the zero row inside their compositions -- run on 1.5 / 0.0, -1.5 / 0.0, 0.0 / 0.0 and the `//` and `%` cases in Main.idr.

idris.name: lexp_7_4__guarded
idris.note: `/` on two Ints with the divisor test decided: the trap on a zero divisor, else the Float quotient.

idris.name: lexp_7_5__float_floordiv
idris.note: `//` with a Float operand takes the zero row first: the IEEE quotient a / b on a zero divisor, else [LEXP.7.5]'s composition.

idris.name: lexp_7_6__float_mod
idris.note: `%` with a Float operand takes the zero row first: NaN on a zero divisor, else [LEXP.7.6]'s composition.
